meera: heads-up: saw a small cluster of double-counted quota events around 16:02 UTC for a handful of origins. looks like stale claim labels after token expiry.
dan: can you paste a log snippet? project keys or ephemeral SA?
meera: ephemeral SA. sample: `auth-proxy: tok=ts_9b2 claim=0x7a3 ttl=20s cache=90s` -> cache > ttl so same claim used after expiry.
ivy: that explains requests > tokens on the quota dashboard. quick mitigation: add a `claim_checksum` label to proxy request metrics and emit `auth_proxy_claim_relabel_count` when we detect a rewrite.
sam: agree. rollout plan: feature flag `auth.proxy.claim_labels` default off, canary at 1% traffic, monitor 30m. if `auth_proxy_claim_relabel_count` > 0, increase sampling and hold.
dan: promql to detect mismatch: `sum by (claim_checksum) (increase(api_requests_total{handler="proxy"}[5m])) > sum by (claim_checksum) (increase(token_issued_total[5m]))` will flag suspect claims.
ivy: UX: show a subtle warning on the quota row when requests/issued > 1 with link to quick runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/claim-ttl-cache.md
meera: gating: require canary error rate < 0.1% and no P50 latency regression. if relabels occur, escalate to 10% sampling for that origin and capture full traces.
dan: i'll open the PR with the label, metric, and flag. will include the prometheus rule and dashboard annotation.
deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-proxy/canary -> k8s-redwood/us-east-1 (id: deploy-2026-05-15-001) :rocket:
ivy: i'll run the promql in staging and post a quick screenshot in ~20m. thanks all :thumbsup:
